findings: The archive held no photorealistic 3D Tiles bodies: those were streamed live (terms forbid caching). What it holds is 68 Google 2D satellite tiles (1.9 MB), two 0.25 m Solar API tiles of the Drillfield, and 180 free AWS terrain tiles (64 at z3). Grade C (counted here).

The bundled XSD requires a GeoOrigin whenever a GeoLOD has inline rootNode children (validator hint, x3d_mcp fa5dccf), although ISO 19775-1 makes it optional. This build uses rootUrl for the low-detail mesh, so no GeoOrigin is needed. Grade C.

X_ITE streams GeoLOD levels frame by frame: about 5 s per level at 4 to 5 fps, but about 100 s per level at 0.5 fps once the Drillfield DSM (shadows on) is in view on SwiftShader. Streaming speed is frame-bound, so the numbers on a real GPU will differ. Grade C for the two measurements, S for any GPU figure.

3D Tiles child transforms are relative to the parent; writing absolute ones makes the round trip fail. The converter's ENU check found 112 of 132 tiles off-axis until the exporter wrote relative transforms, 0 after. Grade C.

GeoLOD has exactly four child slots; a 3D Tiles node with more children is chunked into extra GeoLOD levels (5 chunked nodes here: the synthetic root over the 20 z7 tiles and its chunks). Refine ADD is treated as REPLACE and warned. Grade L.

Heights: GD uses ellipsoid height; the build adds -32.6 m (geoid undulation near Blacksburg, from the planet-scale build) to terrarium ASL heights. Terrarium z15 reads 625.69 m at the Burruss stub and 623.01 m at the Drillfield origin (bilinear, one method). Grade L.

X_ITE has no native 3D Tiles loader (as the GCP plan inferred); the converter is the bridge. X3DOM's GeoTileset (Plesch, Havele, McCann, Aug 2026, per the GCP plan) is the Consortium's own answer and was not tested here. Grade S.

The Drillfield finale is lifted 8 m (DRILL_LIFT in build.py): terrarium z15 reads 623 to 626 m on the field while the DSM ground sits near 617 to 620, which buried the field under the terrain; the east edge is still partly buried. A registration choice, not a survey. Grade S.
